headline: The AI sell off spread to every chip stock and to the power names, and oil closed at $113, yet money ran into bonds and medical devices: the 10 year fell below 5% for the first time in a month.
summary: The dashboard has Thursday Oct 22 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-22), so verdicts, zones and levels below are current to that close. Thursday was the worst day for chips since July: the chip index fell 6.72% with all 30 members down, the Nasdaq fell 2.60% to 26,008.86 and the S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,663.43. Brent settled up about 4% at $113.17, its highest close since May 4, but bonds rallied anyway and the 10 year closed near 4.97%, which says investors fear a slowdown more than inflation. Bloom Energy beat and raised again but burned $181 million of cash, and American Express and SLB beat this morning. Moody's decision on France is not out yet; it is due after the US close today. The dashboard still has no swing or put setups, and no put idea passes.

regime.why: Selling moved from the AI buyers to their suppliers: chip equipment, memory and power gear all fell 6% to 12% on heavy volume. Bonds, health care and defense rose, so money is hiding, not leaving. Oil above $110 and a big earnings and Fed week ahead argue for patience, not bargain hunting.

signals.title: Chips had their worst day since July: Lam warned of shortages into 2027, Nvidia's CEO said neocloud buyers are short of cash, and Meta's filing showed $825 billion of commitments
signals.since_yesterday: Yesterday's sell off of the reporters spread to every supplier: the chip index fell 6.72% and Meta's 10-Q put its future commitments at about $825 billion.
signals.what_happened: The Philadelphia chip index fell 6.72% on Oct 22 to 10,731.98, its weakest close since July 29, with all 30 members down (24/7 Wall St.). Lam's CEO said clean room space and component shortages will limit chipmakers into 2027, and LRCX fell 11.8% to 230.15 on 2.55x normal volume (dashboard). Nvidia's Jensen Huang said demand is strong but neocloud customers lack the working capital to fund their growth; NVDA fell 4.4% to 212.21, AMD 8.1% to 507.93 and MRVL 8.7% to 223.47. Meta's 10-Q showed about $825 billion of future lease and contract commitments, up from about $700 billion in July, and its five year credit default swap hit a record. META closed down 7.0% at 648.85 on 2.01x volume. After the close Western Digital beat (revenue $4.38 billion, up 55%) and guided to 66% to 72% growth, but fell about 6% after hours.
signals.so_what: The first day punished the big buyers; the second day punished the sellers of picks and shovels. Who pays: Meta and the neoclouds, now funding AI with new shares, leases and debt. Who gets paid: chip and tool makers, but Lam just said the scarce thing is clean room space and parts, not demand. When the buyer's credit costs rise (Meta's CDS) and the supplier says it cannot ship faster, the market stops paying a premium for next year's growth. What would make this wrong: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon raising 2027 spending next week with cash, not debt. That is the test.
signals.for_you: Swing: none; no AI chip setups, and you do not buy a 6.7% index drop on day one. Long term: NVDA (212.21, zone 197.15 to 229.36) and MRVL (223.47, zone 218.04 to 250.06) slipped from 'Buy zone now' to 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' on Oct 22 closes; AMD is 'wait for the chart' too. MSFT moved into 'Buy zone now' at 521.08 but reports Oct 28: wait for the report. Puts: none; AI names report next week.

signals.title: Bloom Energy beat and raised for the third time but burned $181 million of cash; power stocks fell hard, with GE Vernova down 10.6% on heavy volume
signals.what_happened: Bloom Energy (BE) after Thursday's close: revenue $1.24 billion, up 138%; product revenue crossed $1 billion for the first time; adjusted EPS $0.94 against about $0.69 expected; 2026 revenue guidance raised to $4.4 to $4.6 billion, the third raise this year (company release, Investing.com). But free cash flow was negative $181 million in the quarter (positive $42 million for the year) as inventory and receivables grew; the CFO said it is not the start of a trend. BE had already fallen 8.7% to 217.77 on Oct 22 and fell about 5% more after hours. The same day GE Vernova fell 10.6% to 827.42 on 2.56x normal volume, Vertiv 7.8%, Eaton 6.3% and Vistra 9.8% (dashboard), as Meta's spending stoked worries about how AI sites get financed (24/7 Wall St.). Comfort Systems (FIX) posted a record $17.81 billion backlog, up from $14.06 billion in June, yet fell 8.7% in the session and about 5% after hours.
signals.so_what: Orders are not the problem: Bloom's sales more than doubled and Comfort's backlog jumped $3.75 billion in a quarter. The problem is who pays and when. Bloom is carrying inventory and receivables for customers who are themselves stretched, which is the same funding worry Huang raised. Power gear was the crowded safe way to own AI; it is now being sold like AI. The scarce thing (grid power) is still scarce, so this looks like a valuation reset, not a broken story, unless orders slow.
signals.for_you: Swing: none. Long term: GEV dropped from 'Buy zone now' to Wait (827.42, below its 909.45 zone bottom) and reports Oct 28 before the open: no new position before then. BE is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' at 217.77 (zone 212.29 to 238.53), sellers lead (0.82): wait. Puts: none on power names this week. BE and FIX are left out of both lists because strong numbers met weak cash or a weak reaction.

signals.title: Brent closed at $113.17, its highest since May, but the 10 year fell below 5%: bonds are betting oil slows the economy
signals.since_yesterday: Brent settled up about 4% at $113.17 and the 10 year fell about 17 basis points to near 4.97%; a report says Trump held back Israeli strikes on Iran until after the Nov 3 midterms.
signals.what_happened: Brent for December settled up about 4% at $113.17 on Oct 22, its highest close since May 4, and WTI rose 2.4% to $99.47, after the deadly Saudi attacks and the US order for some diplomats to leave (Bloomberg via Rigzone). Kpler showed Hormuz flows near prewar levels, so this is a risk premium, not lost barrels. The 10 year yield fell more than 17 basis points to about 4.97%, its first close below 5% since Sep 23 (CNBC), and futures put the odds of a Fed hold on Oct 28 at 92% (Investing.com, Oct 22). The Financial Times reported that Israel planned a multi day campaign against Iran around Oct 10 and Trump delayed it until after the Nov 3 midterms. This morning SLB beat: revenue $9.45 billion, up 6% from a year ago, adjusted EPS $0.64 against $0.62 expected, Middle East revenue up 13% from Q2.
signals.so_what: Oil up and yields down on the same day is the bond market saying high fuel will hurt growth more than it lifts inflation. Who pays: airlines, truckers and consumers. Who gets paid: US producers and service firms like SLB, whose Middle East work is growing. The midterm report matters: if strikes are only on hold until Nov 3, the oil premium has a reason to stay into November. What would make this wrong: a real ceasefire, which would take $10 or more off Brent quickly.

signals.title: Money ran into medical devices on the sell off: Intuitive rose 3.7%, Zimmer and Insulet over 4%; Moderna and Merck's melanoma vaccine data leaked and Moderna fell about 18%
signals.since_yesterday: ISRG rose 3.7% to 443.85 and ABT 2.0% to 102.51, while DXCM fell another 2.4% on 2.66x volume. New: the intismeran melanoma data leaked before Saturday's presentation.
signals.what_happened: On Oct 22 medtech rose while tech fell (dashboard): ISRG up 3.7% to 443.85 (up/down 1.38), ZBH 4.2% to 98.81, PODD 4.4% to 148.12, MDT 3.8% to 96.59, LIVN 3.6% to 81.27 and ABT 2.0% to 102.51. DXCM fell 2.4% to 78.32 on 2.66x normal volume with sellers leading (0.91), a week before its Oct 29 report. Separately, a news site published embargoed data early: Moderna and Merck's personalized vaccine intismeran with Keytruda cut the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% against Keytruda alone, with 82.2% of patients alive and cancer free at two years against 70% (CNBC, BioPharma Dive). Overall survival is not mature. Moderna fell about 18% to 20% and Merck 1.8% in a sell the news move. Full data comes Saturday Oct 24 at ESMO in Madrid.
signals.so_what: Clinically, a 42% cut in recurrence on top of Keytruda in resected melanoma is a strong result; the stock fell because it had risen about 587% this year on the August topline, and survival data and a 2027 filing are still ahead. For devices, the bid is about safety: procedure volumes do not care about AI capex. The second order point: if Keytruda combos extend into more adjuvant settings, Merck protects its biggest drug as its patent ages. One data caution: the dashboard now rates ISRG Wait (116% above fair value) only because the $450 million antitrust settlement made earnings look like they fell 24%; on an adjusted basis EPS rose to $3.00 from $2.40.
signals.for_you: Long term: ZBH (98.81, zone 92.34 to 97.86), PODD (148.12) and LIVN (81.27, zone 70.21 to 80.89) are 'Buy zone now'; ZBH and LIVN closed just above their zone tops, so add only on a dip back into the zone. cycle.quadrant: Inflation rising, growth starting to wobble
cycle.quadrant_why: Inflation: September CPI was 3.7% (Oct 14) and Brent closed at $113.17 on Oct 22. Growth: the bond market now doubts it; the 10 year fell about 17 basis points to near 4.97% on a day oil rose 4%. Spending still holds (American Express billed business up 8%), but AI buyers are funding with leases and new shares.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Late. The Fed is at 3.75% to 4.00% after a September hike; futures put a hold on Oct 28 at 92% (Oct 22). Credit is getting pricier at the top: Meta's five year credit default swap hit a record on Oct 22.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. France's 10 year is at 5.07% with Moody's ruling tonight, and governments are paying more to borrow while private AI spending leans on debt and leases.
cycle.big_cycle: Four of five forces are active. External order: deadly strikes inside Saudi Arabia and a report that Iran strikes were only delayed until after Nov 3. Internal order: the Nov 3 US vote and French unrest. Debt and money: record Meta CDS and sovereign yields near 5%. Technology: the AI build continues, but its suppliers are now repricing.
tailwinds: The 10 year fell below 5% (about 4.97%), easing borrowing costs.
American Express says card spending grew 8%; the consumer is still spending.
Bloom and Comfort Systems show AI power orders are still growing fast.
headwinds: Chips fell 6.72% with all 30 members down; the sell off has spread to suppliers.
Brent closed at $113.17, its highest since May.
Meta's credit costs hit a record and Nvidia's CEO says some buyers lack cash.

history.when: 2000 to 2002, the dot com and telecom build out
history.what: The Nasdaq fell from 5,048.62 on March 10, 2000 to 1,114.11 on Oct 9, 2002, about 78%. Internet use kept growing, but builders had funded capacity with debt and new stock, and suppliers were hit hardest.
history.lesson: When buyers pay for capacity with leases and new shares, suppliers get repriced first. Thursday's chip and power sell off fits that pattern; it is not yet proof of a top.

history.what: Oil peaked at about $147 a barrel in July 2008 while growth was already slowing, and the price then collapsed as demand fell.
history.lesson: When oil rises and bond yields fall together, the bond market is betting high fuel will hurt demand. That bet was right in 2008.

cycle.differences: The 2019 Abqaiq comparison is swapped for 2008 because the story changed from a supply shock to a growth scare: oil rose and yields fell on the same day. What is different from 2008: banks are not the weak point; the leverage is in AI builders and governments. What is different from 2000: the biggest buyers still have huge revenue, and power is a real physical shortage.
cycle.for_you: Swing: none; wait for setups to come back with volume. Puts: none this week; premiums are near the VIX 20 line, but most names you would want report inside a November expiry. Long term: small tranches only in 'Buy zone now' names, after checking each report date; skip names that report next week, such as MSFT.
